newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil deputies resume voting civil service bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil deputies resume voting civil service bill.

text.p: A committee in Brazil's Chamber of Deputies began voting on proposed alterations to the civil service reform bill it approved last week, an official said Wednesday.
If the process of voting on the alterations is concluded this week, as government leaders hope, the bill would be sent to the floor of the lower house October 30, he said.

In an attempt to speed up passage of the reform, the government has withdrawn 14 alterations it had sought to add to the bill at committee level, leaving only seven from opposition parties to be voted on, the official said.

The principle aim of the reform is to allow states and municipalities spending more than 60 percent of receipts on pay to dismiss currently unsackable staff. It would also set a salary limit of 10,800 reais a month for civil servants.
Deputies and senators were reported to be pressuring the government to exempt them from the ceiling.
Newspapers said the group included over 140 members of parliament from both houses and its proposed exemption clause would be floated when the bill reaches the floor of the lower house.
